chunks: I heard Abū al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) saying: When the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) saw Taym, ʿAdiyy, and Banī Umayyah ascending his pulpit, it horrified him. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down Qur'an by which he would be consoled:
And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' so they prostrated except Iblīs; he refused.
Then He revealed to him: O Muḥammad, I commanded but was not obeyed, so do not grieve if you command and are not obeyed concerning your successor.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ: Abū al-Ḥasan, the Imam cited as the speaker in the report
key_terms.إِبْلِيسَ: Iblīs, who refused the command to prostrate
key_terms.اسْجُدُوا: prostrate, the divine command given to the angels
key_terms.قُرْآنًا: Qur'an, revealed here as a source of consolation
key_terms.مِنْبَرَهُ: his pulpit, symbolizing the Prophet’s authority and position
key_terms.وَصِيِّكَ: your successor, the one designated after you

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the Prophet’s grief over opposition to his appointed successor?
ai.summary: This narration presents the Prophet's grief upon seeing certain clans ascend his pulpit and explains that Allah consoled him through the example of Iblīs refusing a divine command. Its significance is in framing disobedience to the Prophet regarding his وصيّ as part of a broader pattern of refusal against divinely mandated authority.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from the one who informed him, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> who said, ‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> saw (in a dream), the Clans of Taym and Aday and the Clan of Umayya riding his<sup>saww</sup> Pulpit, it made him<sup>saww</sup> feel terrible. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Revealed Quran to Comfort him<sup>saww</sup> by it
[2:34] And when We said to the Angels: Prostrate to Adam! So they (all) Prostrated except for Iblees. He refused

. 
Then He<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto him<sup>saww</sup>: “O Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>! I<sup>azwj</sup> Commanded, but they did not obey, so you<sup>saww</sup> should not be anxious when you<sup>saww</sup> command and they do not obey you<sup>saww</sup> regarding your<sup>saww</sup> successor<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 73. Muhammad in Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from al-Husayn ibn Na‘im al-Sahhaf who has said the following. “I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the words of Allah. “. . some of you have accepted the faith and some of you have not. .” [64:2] The Imam (a.s.) said, “Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, has defined their faith through their love for us. He has defined their disbelief in the same fact. This took place on the day He asked all the offspring of Adam (in the form of minute beings) to make a covenant.”

I then asked him about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious. “Obey God and the Messenger, but if you turn away, know that the only duty of Our Messenger is to clearly preaCh” [64:12].

The Imam (a.s.) said, “By Allah, no one of those who were destroyed before or those who will be destroyed up to the time of the rise of al-Mahdi with Divine Authority but because of disregarding of our Wilaya (Leadership with Divine Authority) and the denial of our rights. The Messenger of Allah did not leave this world before establishing the great responsibility on this ’Umma to observe our rights. Allah guides to the right path whomever he wants.”
